key_insight: Embedding-map distance alone is not a reliable guide to plausible, future-relevant LLM ideas: far-off targets resist text generation, and sparse regions poorly predict subsequent growth.
engineering_relevance: Ideation systems should not use embedding distance or sparsity as standalone objectives for novelty or research promise.
method: Tested whether LLM-generated text can reach random far points and interior gaps in embedding space.
Evaluated whether past-map gap scores predict later growth in Steam, arXiv and patent datasets.
Compared LLM continuations with real follow-ups and tested critique, directional feedback and distance-graded inspiration.
evidence_signal: Neighbour-free search reached interior gaps at median cosine similarities of 0.57 and 0.47 but far points at only 0.07 and 0.06; gap-score growth forecasts yielded AUCs of 0.30–0.66.
watch_item: Original tests were registered before execution, but follow-ups came after the main results, and all registration dates rely only on local git commits.
paper_title: Do Embedding-Map Distances Guide LLM Ideation? Four Tests Against What Came Next
